figure: FIGURE 3.4 (Dense vs MoE parameter allocation and KV cache behavior), right 'MoE (8 experts)' column
issue: The numeral '11.4' is used with two different units in the same column, creating a notation trap. In the legend it is a per-expert weight size in GB ('inactive experts ≈ 68 GB (6 × 11.4)' and 'active experts ≈ 23 GB resident (2 × 11.4)'), but in the per-token line it is an active parameter count in billions ('per token: 11.4B top-2 + 1.4B always-on = 12.8B → 25.6 GB'). A reader who carries one unit across both lines will mis-derive the residency or the per-token read.
evidence: Legend: 6 × 11.4 = 68.4 ≈ 68 GB and 2 × 11.4 = 22.8 ≈ 23 GB, so the legend's 11.4 is GB per expert (5.7B params × 2 bytes). Per-token line: 11.4B top-2 = 2 experts × 5.7B params, so the same '11.4' is B-params for two experts. The two '11.4' values are numerically equal but dimensionally different (11.4 GB = one expert; 11.4B params = two experts). The caption confirms the per-expert size as '~11.4B = 2 × 5.7B' (params) and the residency as '~94 GB', which only closes if the legend's 11.4 is read as GB.
acceptance_test: After the fix, every occurrence of '11.4' in Figure 3.4 carries an explicit, distinct unit so a reader can state the quantity of each without the caption: the legend reads e.g. '6 × 11.4 GB' / '2 × 11.4 GB' (per-expert weight) and the per-token line reads '11.4B params (top-2)'. Verify 6×(per-expert GB)≈68 GB, 2×(per-expert GB)≈23 GB, and 11.4B params×2 bytes≈22.8 GB all hold, and that no single unqualified '11.4' remains.

figure: FIGURE 3.4, red summary chips 'dense 12 GB vs MoE 0.6 GB' (both columns)
issue: The red chips state concrete KV sizes (12 GB / 0.6 GB) and the precision (8-bit) and the attention shapes, but omit the context length at which those sizes are evaluated. The figure alone therefore under-specifies the operating point; the 9.2K anchor exists only in the caption.
evidence: Chip text: 'dense 12 GB vs MoE 0.6 GB / 8-bit KV set by shape, not routing: 80L/8192H MHA vs 32L/4096H GQA' — no token count. The line above only says 'KV grows linearly with context'. The caption supplies the missing anchor: '1.31 MB/token (dense 80L/8192H full-MHA) vs 0.0655 MB/token (challenger 32L/4096H GQA) at 8-bit, i.e. ~12 GB vs ~0.6 GB for the 9.2K input.' 1.31 MB × 9200 ≈ 12.05 GB and 0.0655 MB × 9200 ≈ 0.60 GB, confirming the chips are 9.2K values.
acceptance_test: After the fix, the red chip (or an adjacent in-figure line) states the context length, e.g. 'at 9.2K tokens, 8-bit', so a reader of the figure alone can reproduce 1.31 MB/token × 9.2K ≈ 12 GB and 0.0655 MB/token × 9.2K ≈ 0.6 GB without opening the caption.
